It asserts broad applicability ("any reinforced-concrete structure") before the narrow, concrete evaluation scope (highway overpass decks from two county archives) is even mentioned. Extract the broad claim on its own terms - do not wait to see whether the eventual Results section actually covers that breadth, and do not silently narrow the quote to match the evaluation scope. The first sentence stays unextracted (pure background about how inspectors work, no assertion about EchoDeck). The last sentence is evaluation scope, not a claim, so it is not extracted either - only the middle sentence asserts something about EchoDeck itself.

input_excerpt: Section 1 Introduction. Measuring soil nitrate with laboratory assays requires shipping physical samples and waiting days for each batch of results. That pairing is an implied efficiency-superiority claim against the whole class of laboratory assay workflows - not against the satellite-index baseline actually benchmarked in Section 4, and it carries no number of its own. Extract the Introduction pairing as its own claim even though Results never runs a laboratory-assay timing comparison to back it up; that gap is exactly what audit needs to see. The Results sentence is a separate, narrower claim (against a specific tested baseline) and must be extracted too - the two are not interchangeable and will be audited differently.
